summary: The substantive D-056 Class-B route is supportable: D-006 supplies the D-002-slice architecture decision; measurement remains condition 4 / DR-012; DR-118 is excluded; the Blueprint hard-blocker is replaced; no qualification, implementation authority, D-088 reversal, or stale 1-of-30 snapshot survives. Three record-quality defects prevent CONSENT. The eligibility recital states globally that no undecided numbers remain even though D-006 and live file 08 retain future G05 caps and outside-slice numerics; that claim needs explicit architecture-preview scoping. The recital also reintroduces the rejected 'countable subset' terminology instead of D-086/D-088's canonical 'presently recordable required' vocabulary. Finally, the exact condition-2 replacement is not delimited as one literal because its internal Markdown backticks are unescaped.

objections.title: The no-undecided-numbers recital outruns D-006's recorded scope
objections.claim: Eligibility item 2 says without qualification that 'No undecided numbers remain,' but the governing live record preserves numeric decisions outside the current D-002 architecture-preview scope.
evidence: D-006 is expressly scoped to the D-002 slice's platforms and DR-G01..G05; it decides G05 measurement and visibility with no numeric cap in that decision, and routes caps to the first component-acceptance decision.
The live file-08 gate preamble says numerics for gates outside the D-002 slice remain open under DR-115.
D-006 also routes exact G03/G04 machine identifiers, OS versions, and cache-state protocol to a later reviewed D-006-conforming harness-naming act with product sign-off.

D-056 is itself scoped to architecture preview and identifies DR-115 as eligible in kind. That supports this D-089 route for current preview scope, but does not support an unbounded claim that every future or outside-slice numeric decision is closed.
objections.impact: The operative decision is mostly scoped correctly, but the absolute recital can be read as silently closing future G05 caps, outside-slice numerics, or G03/G04 naming work when the governing records preserve them. That weakens the proof that D-056 Eligibility (2) is being applied only to current architecture-preview acceptance evidence.
objections.requiredRepair: Qualify the recital to the D-002 architecture-preview scope. State expressly that D-006 supplies DR-115's current decision half; future G05 caps and outside-slice numerics remain open under their recorded triggers and are not closed by D-089; G03/G04 exact pins remain a separate D-006-conforming condition-4 naming obligation, not a DR-115 threshold co-authoring act. Preserve those caveats in the adopted summary.

objections.title: The recital reintroduces the rejected countable-subset vocabulary
objections.claim: Eligibility item 3 says D-088 recorded identifiers for 'the countable subset,' while adopted D-086 deliberately replaced that counting language with 'presently recordable required identifiers.'
evidence: Adopted D-086 records D086-SF-1 as accepted and its operative rider uses 'presently recordable required identifiers'; it also fixes the denominator at 18 and keeps G03/G04 required and unnamed.
Adopted D-088 and live file 08 use the same 16-of-18 required-gate account and do not describe the named set as a separate countable denominator.
D-089's following sentence and readiness effect preserve G03/G04 and 16 of 18, so this is terminology drift rather than an actual denominator change.
objections.impact: A new authoritative decision would revive wording previously removed because it can imply that unnamed required gates fall outside the denominator, despite the subject's otherwise-correct 16-of-18 account.
objections.requiredRepair: Replace 'recorded identifiers for the countable subset' with the adopted vocabulary, such as 'recorded identifiers for the presently recordable required subset,' and preferably name G01/G02/G05 in the DR-115-local recital while retaining G03/G04 as required and unnamed.

objections.title: The exact condition-2 replacement is not quoted as one literal
objections.claim: The replacement text beginning at subject line 68 opens an inline-code span and then immediately terminates it at the unescaped backtick before SATISFIED; subsequent status-token backticks fragment the supposed exact literal.
evidence: The raw subject uses `**2 of 30 `SATISFIED`** ... `OPEN` ...` with an outer backtick and unescaped inner backticks.
The adopted D-085 predecessor presented the same kind of exact snapshot literal with each internal status-token backtick escaped, making the complete replacement unambiguous.
The intended arithmetic is correct: changing DR-115 yields 2 SATISFIED, 22 OPEN, 4 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, and 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW. The defect is literal delimitation, not the count.
objections.impact: D-089 labels these bytes an exact MF-6 edit, but the frozen Markdown does not encode the whole replacement as one literal, creating avoidable ambiguity for manual or automated application.
objections.requiredRepair: Escape every internal backtick as in D-085 turn 3, or place the complete desired Measured-now cell in a fenced code block, then freeze and re-dispatch.
